A0223.title: Device Vendor Security Capability Integration
A0223.definition: Integrating device-trust and runtime-environment attestation capabilities provided by OS or platform vendors, leveraging vendor-backed hardware-level and system-level trust assertions to verify device authenticity and runtime-environment integrity.
A0223.description: Device manufacturer security capability integration refers to accessing the official device trust and runtime environment verification interfaces provided by OS/platform manufacturers. The manufacturer performs the assessment at the hardware root of trust or system kernel layer and returns a trust conclusion to the business side. Typical capabilities include: iOS DeviceCheck and App Attest, Google Play Integrity API (formerly SafetyNet Attestation), manufacturer-adapted Trusted Execution Environments (TEE), WeChat Mini Program getUserRiskRank, HarmonyOS NEXT SafetyDetect, Xiaomi device trusted service data signature verification, OPPO terminal environment security detection, vivo Qianjing Trusted Engine, and others. Unlike pure software-layer device fingerprinting (A0021) and terminal application hardening (A0013), the assessment logic of manufacturer security capabilities runs at the manufacturer-controlled hardware root of trust or system privileged layer, making it difficult for attackers to forge or hook on the terminal side, with bypass costs significantly higher than software fingerprinting. Additionally, manufacturers possess a global device risk profile and can identify abnormal environments such as root, unlocked bootloader, hooking frameworks, device farms, and emulators. This method is often used as a hardware-level enhancement for device fingerprinting (A0021) and abnormal environment detection (A0010), improving the overall trustworthiness and bypass resistance of device identification.
A0223.limitation: Manufacturer security capabilities depend on the device manufacturer ecosystem and system version, resulting in limited coverage (e.g., devices without the manufacturer's service framework, jailbroken/rooted devices, or custom ROM devices may be unable to invoke the capability or the results may be untrusted). The interfaces and assessment criteria vary across manufacturers, requiring multi-vendor adaptation and incurring high integration costs for the business side. Some capabilities are subject to privacy compliance constraints and return a risk level rather than a unique device identifier, making them difficult to use directly for unique device tracking. The availability and stability of manufacturer services also impact business continuity.
